summary: Updates IANA registry rules for the Telephony Routing over IP (TRIP) protocol so postal addresses no longer have to be included in contact information. It updates RFC 3219 and is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8602 changes the TRIP registry rules so IANA no longer collects postal addresses when adding entries. It also directs that previously collected addresses be removed.

questions: what did rfc 8602 change in trip registries
subtitle: Removes postal address collection from TRIP registry registration rules.

tldr.problem: TRIP registry rules required postal addresses in contact information, although the RFC identifies no use for those addresses.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC updates the registration rules for TRIP Attributes and ITAD Numbers so IANA no longer has to collect postal addresses, and removes previously collected addresses.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8602 updates RFC 3219 and identifies a privacy benefit with no identified security impact.

facts.label: Registries affected
facts.value: TRIP Attributes and TRIP ITAD Numbers

today: RFC 8602 is a Proposed Standard from July 2019 and updates RFC 3219.

sections.title: Why the Rule Changed
sections.content:
The memo updates the IANA registry rules for Telephony Routing over IP (TRIP). It removes the requirement to include postal addresses in contact information.

The RFC identifies no use for the addresses and says omitting them provides a privacy benefit. It updates RFC 3219.
sections.plainLanguage: The TRIP registries had required postal addresses, but this memo identifies no use for them. Removing that requirement reduces the personal information collected.

sections.title: Changes to TRIP Registries
sections.content:
The updated registration rules apply to the TRIP Attributes registry and the TRIP IP Telephony Administrative Domain (ITAD) Numbers registry. The IETF no longer requires IANA to collect postal address information when adding TRIP entries.

IANA has also removed postal addresses that had already been collected from these registries.
sections.plainLanguage: New TRIP entries no longer need a postal address. Addresses already stored in the two registries have been removed.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that no security impacts of this change have been identified. Its stated benefit is privacy through omitting and removing postal address information.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC identifies a privacy benefit and says no security impact has been identified.

references.text: Rosenberg, J., Salama, H., and M. Squire, "Telephony Routing over IP (TRIP)", RFC 3219, January 2002.
